architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards
voi_tool.not_a_posterior: The local design contains six audited realizations and two thermal-hold trajectories. That does not support a calibrated Bayesian expected-information computation, so no posterior probability is fabricated. Weight sensitivity is reported instead.

decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.tie_interpretation: The deterministic VOI layer is indifferent among the tied top experiments: they share an identical component vector. Tie-breaking is therefore a genuine task left to the Agent, and any selection inside this set cannot have been read off the VOI ranking.
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Accept the acrylic-only superlinear-suppression result if the mean SI_15_60 is below 3.80%, which is half of the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction for reactive mass fraction 0.8000. This supports H-RESIN and falsifies both H-CORE and the tackifier-required condition of H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: If mean SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61%, H-RESIN is falsified. If it is below 5.61%, H-CORE is falsified because the result is more than the declared 2.00 percentage points below its 7.61% prediction; within this region, only a result below 3.80% also falsifies H-DUAL. A result from 5.61% through 9.61% remains compatible with H-CORE within measurement resolution, while a result above 9.61% falsifies H-CORE as well as H-RESIN and is not explained by simple near-linear drift.
hypotheses_left_entangled: H-CORE and H-DUAL remain entangled if the acrylic-only result is near the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run the matched-window 120 C hold on the corresponding dual-axis composition containing 20% acrylic-like modifier and 5% minor tackifier-like modifier, again with at least two independent preparations. The with-versus-without-tackifier contrast determines whether tackifier addition restores low drift when the acrylic-only result falsifies H-RESIN, or whether tackifier supplies any incremental suppression when acrylic alone falsifies H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: Arithmetic mean across at least two independent preparations of SI_15_60 = 100 * (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, during the matched-window 120 C hold.
judge_normalized.rationale: S1C49 under the direct 120 C hold is scientifically defensible and maximizes hypothesis separation rather than immediate mitigation. Its 20% acrylic-only composition can show whether low drift is attainable without minor tackifier: below 3.80% favors formulation-level superlinear suppression and falsifies the tackifier-required hypothesis, whereas drift at or above 7.61% falsifies strong acrylic-only suppression and motivates the matched dual-axis contrast. No molecular mechanism is inferred.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator rather than the Proposer. The Proposer's S1C51 dual-axis card has the highest tied deterministic VOI and is better framed as a mitigation candidate, but it necessarily leaves H-RESIN versus H-DUAL entangled. The acrylic-only S1C49 card directly tests H-DUAL's defining falsification condition and better answers the stated three-way scientific question. This design-level discrimination benefit justifies departing from the stable deterministic top set.

uncertainty_decomposition.evidence_coverage_uncertainty: The 20% acrylic-like level is inside the stated supported region, but source-level external-prior queries returned no rows, modifier reactive functionality is unverified, and any NCO-reactive contribution could invalidate the nominal reactive-mass-fraction benchmark.
uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: Composition-space extrapolation is low because 20% acrylic-like modifier is directly anchored, but transfer from analogue evidence and the original local chemistry to this acrylic-only formulation remains uncertain.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: The matched-window observable is direct and has a declared 2.00 percentage-point discrimination threshold, but the E1-derived 7.61% benchmark comes from a single original hold run. The decision uses the arithmetic mean of at least two independent S1C49 preparations.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: M-HOLD-120 does not control realization state, and E2 exhibited a 3.5688-fold between-preparation viscosity spread at 120 C. Preparation and process history must therefore be controlled and recorded; discordant repeats remain a material risk.

planner.failure_mode: Formulation-dependent viscosity growth during prolonged 120 °C melt residence, with the mechanism of drift suppression unresolved.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original 120 °C thermal-hold measurements show a 15–60 min viscosity increase of 51.54% for E5, versus 9.51% for the least-drifting original reference E1.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Only E1 and E5 have local 120 °C hold trajectories, each represented by one four-point run over 15–90 min; the registered decision window of 15–60 min therefore lacks independent repeats and systematic coverage of the acrylic-like and minor tackifier-like axes. In contrast, temperature response is measured at six temperatures from 80 to 130 °C across several formulations and runs, and realized viscosity-level variability is directly documented for E2 with three runs at each temperature.
measurement_requirements: Use the matched-window 120 °C hold protocol: measure viscosity at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min and report SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 as a percent.

Run at least two independent preparations per tested composition and preserve preparation and process-history records so drift differences are not silently attributed to formulation when realization state differs.

Include contrasts capable of separating modifier mechanisms: an acrylic-only composition and a composition with a non-zero minor tackifier-like fraction, preferably at matched or interpretable reactive-core fractions.

For every tested composition, calculate the preregistered H-CORE linear-dilution prediction from E1 drift and the reactive mass fraction, then compare measured drift with that prediction using the declared 2 percentage-point matched-window resolution.

Treat drift below half of the linear-dilution prediction as the preregistered evidence threshold for H-RESIN, while testing H-DUAL by whether an acrylic-only composition can or cannot enter the low-drift regime.

Measure the realized viscosity level within the supported 80–130 °C range, including a 110 °C state anchor with direct 120 and 130 °C checks, so drift suppression is not conflated with an uncontrolled displacement of viscosity scale.
Do not infer molecular reaction pathways from rheology alone; use the measurements only to adjudicate the registered formulation-level rheological hypotheses.
planner.scientific_question: At matched 120 °C residence time, do acrylic-like and minor tackifier-like modifiers reduce viscosity drift only in proportion to dilution of the reactive core, suppress drift substantially beyond linear dilution, or require a non-zero minor tackifier fraction to reach the low-drift regime?

hypotheses_not_separated: H-RESIN vs H-DUAL: both predict approximately 3.57% drift for this dual-axis composition, so this experiment cannot distinguish them

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: Drift below 3.57% across at least two repeats establishes suppression beyond half of the 7.13% linear-dilution prediction, accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE, and is also consistent with H-DUAL. It does not distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: Drift at or above 7.13% falsifies H-RESIN. Agreement with 7.13% within the declared 2 percentage-point resolution supports H-CORE; a result substantially above that range would instead indicate that neither simple linear dilution nor superlinear suppression adequately describes the outcome. This dual-axis result alone does not meet the registered acrylic-only falsification condition for H-DUAL.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result between 3.57% and 7.13% would not meet the stringent H-RESIN acceptance threshold. A value more than 2 percentage points below 7.13% would reject H-CORE without cleanly accepting the registered strong-suppression criterion, whereas a value within measurement resolution of 7.13% would remain compatible with H-CORE. An acrylic-only hold would still be required to adjudicate H-RESIN against H-DUAL.

proposer.primary_observable: Directly measured SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, during a 120 C hold

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: It has identical deterministic VOI and lower modifier burden, but its 15% acrylic level is only directional lower-region evidence with an unverified literature denominator, whereas 20% is directly commensurate.
It has identical deterministic VOI, but 17.5% acrylic is an interpolated in-region level rather than a direct external anchor.
It has identical deterministic VOI, but 22.5% acrylic is interpolated and adds modifier burden without increasing hypothesis-pair discrimination.
Its 25% acrylic level is directly supported, but it is a larger perturbation from the characterized local chemistry and provides no additional discrimination over the 20% point.
It provides the same pairwise discrimination but uses 7.5% minor tackifier, outside the repeated 4.8-6.4% cluster, producing nonzero extrapolation risk and a lower VOI.

proposer.reasoning: The matched-window hold directly measures the least-resolved and decision-relevant failure coordinate without a regression or transfer model. S1C51 lies inside both externally supported intervention regions, separates two of the three registered hypothesis pairs, and uses directly anchored 20% acrylic and 5% tackifier levels. Its principal limitation is moderate process-state risk and its inability to separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL; independent repeats and recorded preparation histories are therefore essential.
proposer.tie_break_justification: S1C51 combines 20% acrylic-like modifier, a directly commensurate external evidence anchor, with 5% minor tackifier-like modifier, which lies in the repeatedly documented 4.8-6.4% cluster. It therefore has stronger two-axis intervention support than the 15% directional point or the interpolated 17.5% and 22.5% points, while imposing less modifier burden than the directly supported 25% acrylic point.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: Replace S1C51 as the standalone experiment with the corresponding 20% acrylic-like, 0% minor-tackifier acrylic-only candidate S1C49 under M-HOLD-120, ideally run as a paired contrast with S1C51. This directly targets the H-RESIN versus H-DUAL distinction that all five tied top experiments leave unresolved. Prespecify replicate aggregation, control and record preparation history, verify modifier reactive functionality and recalculate NCO:OH, and include the planned realized-viscosity state checks.
residual_decision_risk: A single acrylic-only result still does not provide the complete with-versus-without-tackifier comparison as strongly as a paired S1C49/S1C51 design.
M-HOLD-120 does not itself control realization state, despite the documented 3.5688-fold E2 between-preparation spread at 120 C.
The linear-dilution benchmark inherits unquantified uncertainty from the single-run E1 reference.
Modifier OH or other NCO-reactive functionality could invalidate nominal reactive-mass-fraction and stoichiometric comparisons unless verified.
The repeat aggregation rule and treatment of discordant or borderline repeats remain unspecified.
Rheological drift alone cannot establish a molecular reaction pathway or the claimed encounter-frequency mechanism.
Weight perturbations beyond the reported 0.5x to 1.5x sweep were not evaluated.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection is design-level rather than merely interpretive. Every member of the tied top set is a dual-axis composition and leaves H-RESIN versus H-DUAL entangled. S1C51 can directly test drift against the H-CORE linear-dilution benchmark and the strong-suppression threshold, but it cannot test H-DUAL's defining acrylic-only falsification condition or determine whether the minor tackifier is required. Because the stated scientific question is three-way, the next discriminating measurement should be an acrylic-only 120 C hold, preferably as a paired contrast with S1C51. This scientific coverage issue is not represented adequately by the tied VOI component vectors and justifies departing from the deterministic top set.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The proposed S1C51::M-HOLD-120 remains in the unchanged five-member tied top set under all 25 tested one-term perturbations from 0.5x to 1.5x. Every recommendation_flip_boundary is null and marked as surviving the entire sweep; top_experiment_set_stability is 1.0. Thus no tested weighting, whether scientifically defensible or not, changes the deterministic recommendation. Perturbations outside the tested range were not assessed. The margin to the first strictly lower experiment is only 0.004583, but that lower experiment did not enter the top set anywhere in the reported sweep.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: M-HOLD-120 can directly produce SI_15_60 values at or above 7.13%, thereby meeting the stated H-RESIN falsification criterion, or below 3.57%, thereby meeting the proposal's stringent H-CORE rejection criterion. It cannot produce the registered H-DUAL falsification result because that requires an acrylic-only composition. The protocol should also prespecify replicate aggregation and account for uncertainty in the single-run E1 reference used to calculate 7.13%.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment could be presented as discriminating H-DUAL even though it cannot test the hypothesis's defining tackifier-required condition.
objections.objection: The claimed separation "H-CORE vs H-DUAL" is overstated. For S1C51, the numerical predictions are 7.1325% for H-CORE and 3.5663% for H-DUAL, a 3.5662 percentage-point difference that does exceed the declared 2.0-point resolution. However, the registered H-DUAL falsification condition is specifically that an acrylic-only composition reaches the low-drift regime, and its support condition requires comparing compositions with and without minor tackifier. S1C51 contains both 20% acrylic-like modifier and 5% minor tackifier-like modifier, so no possible result from this one composition can satisfy the registered H-DUAL falsification condition or establish that tackifier is required. The proposer correctly declares H-RESIN versus H-DUAL unseparated, but the same design limitation makes H-CORE versus H-DUAL only prediction-contrast coverage, not full registered-hypothesis adjudication.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Suppression beyond the nominal linear-dilution prediction could be wrongly attributed to a resin-continuum or tackifier-required mechanism when it could instead arise from one modifier alone, an interaction, or altered effective stoichiometry.
objections.objection: S1C51 simultaneously introduces 20% AC1920, 5% TK100, and reduces the reactive-core mass fraction to 0.75. Therefore, any observed suppression cannot be attributed separately to the acrylic-like axis, the minor-tackifier-like axis, or their interaction. In particular, the experiment cannot determine whether acrylic alone suppresses drift, tackifier alone suppresses drift, tackifier is required in the presence of acrylic, or the two modifiers act synergistically. In addition, the E2 anchor notes that true NCO:OH must be recalculated if either modifier has reactive functionality, but the proposed protocol does not require verified OH or other NCO-reactive specifications. If either modifier is reactive, the nominal 0.75 reactive mass fraction is not a sufficient stoichiometric descriptor.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A drift difference may be assigned to formulation even if preparation or realization state changed between repeats or relative to the E1 reference.
objections.objection: The selected M-HOLD-120 plan has controls_process_state=false, process_state_risk=0.75, and six missing process fields. E2 previously showed a 3.5688-fold between-preparation viscosity spread at 120 C. Although the planner requires controlled and recorded process histories and a 110 C state anchor with direct 120 and 130 C checks, the actual selected experiment card specifies only the thermal hold and two independent repeats. Recording histories without prespecified process controls or the planned state checks does not demonstrate matched realization state.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The measured observable remains interpretable, but borderline or discordant replicate results could be adjudicated inconsistently.
objections.objection: The primary observable itself survives this attack surface: SI_15_60 is calculated directly from measured eta_15 and eta_60 during the same 120 C hold and requires no regression, extrapolation, or imputation. The weakness lies only in the decision rule: "across at least two repeats" does not specify whether both repeats must individually satisfy the threshold, whether their mean is used, or how discordant repeats are handled.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The study may be called a falsification test for all three hypotheses even though only H-RESIN and H-CORE have attainable outcome criteria in this experiment, and their threshold precision may be overstated.
objections.objection: The H-RESIN and H-CORE criteria are physically attainable by M-HOLD-120: the protocol can directly return drift at or above 7.13% or below 3.57%. However, the protocol cannot attain the registered H-DUAL falsification condition because S1C51 is not acrylic-only. Also, the 7.13% linear-dilution benchmark is derived from the single E1 hold run, while the declared 2.0 percentage-point resolution is described for the repeated matched-window estimate; uncertainty in the E1-derived benchmark is not incorporated.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A formulation-level rheological outcome could be overinterpreted as evidence for a specific molecular mechanism or modifier-role specialization that the measurement does not observe.
objections.objection: No use of an unmeasured S1C51 outcome is evident in the supplied trace. The scope problem is mechanistic: H-RESIN states that suppression occurs by lowering effective concentration and encounter frequency of reaction-capable species, but M-HOLD-120 measures only viscosity drift and cannot establish encounter frequency or a molecular reaction pathway. Likewise, the H-DUAL statement that acrylic principally relocates viscosity level while tackifier suppresses drift cannot be established by the selected hold measurement alone, especially because the proposed experiment omits the specified state-anchor and temperature-check measurements.

skeptic.recommended_change: Replace the single-composition test with at least a paired 120 C hold design containing S1C51 and an acrylic-only composition, using composition-specific linear-dilution predictions and controlled, recorded preparation histories. Preferably use a 2x2 modifier design with acrylic-like modifier at 0% and 20% and minor tackifier-like modifier at 0% and 5%, with an inert mass-balance control where needed to match reactive-core fraction. Verify modifier reactive functionality and recalculate NCO:OH before testing. Run at least two independent preparations per cell, prespecify how repeats are aggregated, and include the planned realized-viscosity state anchor/direct checks.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The single dual-axis S1C51 experiment cannot test the defining tackifier-required contrast in H-DUAL and simultaneously confounds acrylic, tackifier, and reactive-core dilution. It therefore cannot answer the stated three-way scientific question about whether a non-zero minor tackifier fraction is required.

tool_trace.reason: This must be obtained first to load the upstream material-state structure, shared thermal response, calibration behavior, and hold-drift design rules before any candidate or experiment ranking.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The phosphoric-acid-labelled E1 +P curve is not used in the chemistry-audited primary state model.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

provenance_audit.reason: The source record is phosphoric-acid-labelled and its additive identity/amount is not represented in formulations.csv; it is retained as sensitivity-only until chemistry is reconciled.

result.source_scope: original pre-validation local measurements with chemistry-comparability audit

tool_trace.reason: After the state-aware structure is loaded, this is needed to define the E2 reactive-core anchor, independent modifier axes, historical boundary, and admissible pre-result candidate-space interpretation.

evidence: PAT_US20160215185A1: repeated acrylic tackifying resin examples at approximately 19-20% of total formulation
PAT_US6465104B1 Example 10: 25 wt% low-OH acrylic copolymer with direct 121 C viscosity-stability data
PAPER_CN_ADHESIVES_2025_34_09_54: reports a 15% preferred acrylic-resin addition level, retained as directional lower-bound evidence until its fraction denominator is reverified
acrylic_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 20 and 25% are directly commensurate coarse anchors in the current curated record. The 15% grid level is retained as a lower-bound design point, but the literature denominator for the reported 15% addition level is not treated as an exact total-formulation anchor until reverified.

evidence: PAT_US5932680A: examples around 4.8-6.4% tackifying/hydrocarbon resin and preferred resin range 3-10 wt%
PAT_US20070155859A1: tackifiers/rheology-control agents typically used below about 10 wt%
minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

tool_trace.reason: The full measured E1 trajectory and deterministic descriptors are needed to establish the least-drifting original reference and the baseline used by the linear-dilution prediction.

tool_trace.name: get_hold_stability

tool_trace.name: inspect_formulation
tool_trace.reason: The candidate lattice is anchored to E2, so its reactive-core and modifier fractions must be understood before candidate experiments can be compared.

tool_trace.name: get_repeatability_risk
tool_trace.reason: E2 shows large nominal run spread; its measured repeatability risk is needed to determine how strongly a candidate measurement plan must control preparation state.

tool_trace.name: get_temperature_support
tool_trace.reason: Measured temperature support and response summaries are needed to keep anchor and verification measurements within supported conditions and avoid extrapolation.

tool_trace.name: query_external_priors
tool_trace.reason: The supplied digest contains no acrylic-like entries, so source-level analogue evidence and its limitations are needed before assigning evidential weight to that formulation-family axis.

tool_trace.name: query_external_priors
tool_trace.reason: The supplied digest contains no minor-tackifier entries, so source-level evidence is needed to assess the prior basis and limitations of the tackifier-required hypothesis.

voi_sent_to_model.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi_sent_to_model.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.

top_cards.acceptance_criterion: Matched 15-60 min drift at 120 C stays below 3.80% across at least two repeats, i.e. below half the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61% implied by a reactive mass fraction of 0.8000. This accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE.
top_cards.falsification_criterion: H-RESIN is falsified if matched 15-60 min drift is at or above the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61%. H-CORE is falsified if drift falls below 3.80%, a separation larger than the 2.00% resolution threshold. This composition carries both axes, so it cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL; an acrylic-only hold is the follow-up required for that.

measurement_plan.name: matched-window 120 C thermal hold
measurement_plan.protocol: Hold the melt at 120 C. Record viscosity at 15, 30, 45 and 60 min. Report the 15-60 min matched-window relative change. Run at least two independent repeats.
